main.content:
{{Current events header|2015|05|13}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]: [[Hezbollah]] and [[Syrian Army]] gain strategic territories in [[Qalamoun Mountains]] north of Damascus, which was held by opposition factions, particularly [[al-Nusra Front]]. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2015/05/hezbollah-syria-qalamoun-gains-150513152132369.html (Al Jazeera)]
*Gunmen [[2015 Karachi bus shooting|open fire on a bus]] containing members of the [[Isma'ilism|Ismaili Shia Muslim]] community in the Pakistani city of [[Karachi]], killing at least 44 people and injuring a dozen. [http://tribune.com.pk/story/885511/five-dead-24-injured-in-firing-attack-in-karachi/ (''Pakistan Tribune'')], [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-32717321 (BBC)]
*The [[Government of Iraq]] claims that [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] second-in-command [[Abdul Rahman Mustafa Mohammed]] has been killed in an airstrike in northern Iraq. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-32726646 (BBC)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2015–present)|War in Afghanistan]]: Gunmen attack a [[Kabul]] guesthouse used by both foreigners and locals sparking a gun battle with [[Law enforcement in Afghanistan|police]]. At least eight people including the three gunmen are killed with 16 rescued and 100 still inside. [http://www.trust.org/item/20150513171905-yzk4o/ (Thomson Reuters Foundatiion)], [http://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/american-killed-attack-kabul-guesthouse-n358521 (NBC News)]
*[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)|Yemen crisis]]: A five day truce begins in Yemen as various aid groups, including Iran, seek to gain access to the country's ports and airports. Saudi Arabia had blocked Iranian Red Crescent aids recently. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-32719194 (BBC)]
*A military reservist opens fire at a South Korean military base killing 2 and injuring 3. [http://english.yonhapnews.co.kr/news/2015/05/13/0200000000AEN20150513005453315.html (Yonhap)]

;Business and economy
*Japanese carmakers [[Toyota]] and [[Nissan]] recall 6.5 million vehicles due to fears over exploding [[airbag]]s. [http://news.yahoo.com/toyota-nissan-recall-6-5-mln-cars-over-055536436--finance.html (AFP via Yahoo!)]
*The [[United States Department of Agriculture]] reports that more than 40% of [[Western honey bee|honey bee colonies]] [[Colony collapse disorder|died]] in the preceding year. Farmers rely on honey bees to pollinate over half the country's food supply annually. [http://www.wsj.com/articles/over-40-of-honeybee-colonies-died-in-year-usda-says-1431531544 (''Wall Street Journal'')]
*International conglomerate [[Danaher Corporation|Danaher]] announces plans to acquire water filtration company [[Pall Corporation|Pall]] for US$13.8 billion and to split off its industrial businesses into a new company. [http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-05-13/danaher-to-buy-pall-for-13-8-billion-split-into-two-companies (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Rescue efforts resume in Nepal after [[May 2015 Nepal earthquake|yesterday's earthquake]] which killed at least 63 in Nepal and 17 in northern India. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-32716211 (BBC)], [http://edition.cnn.com/2015/05/12/asia/nepal-earthquake/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2015 Philadelphia train derailment]]
**The death toll from the derailment rises to seven with over 200 people injured. [http://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/local/Amtrak-Derailment-Philadelphia--303536331.html (WCAU)], [http://www.usnews.com/news/articles/2015/05/13/amtrak-northeast-regional-train-crash-in-philadelphia-kills-at-least-6 (US News and World Report'')]
**Search teams recover the [[Train event recorder|black box]]. [http://www.news24.com/news24/World/News/Black-box-recovered-from-Amtrak-train-20150513 (AFP via News24)]
**Reports indicate that train is believed to have been traveling in excess of 100 mph (161 km/h), about twice the speed limit for the curve.[http://www.cnn.com/2015/05/13/us/philadelphia-amtrak-train-derailment/ (CNN)]
*[[2015 Valenzuela fire]]: At least 72 people die after a fire engulfs a rubber sandal factory in [[Valenzuela, Philippines|Valenzuela City]], a northern suburb of [[Manila]], Philippines. [http://www.cnn.com/2015/05/14/asia/philippines-factory-fire/ (CNN)] [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2015/05/dozens-missing-philippines-factory-fire-manila-150513092030065.html (Al-Jazeera)] 
*Rescue workers attempt to rescue at least 15 [[gold mine]]rs trapped by floods in a mine in Colombia's [[Caldas Department]]. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-32732268 (BBC)]

;International relations
*The [[Vatican]] concludes a treaty to recognize the [[State of Palestine|Palestinian state]]. [http://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/14/world/middleeast/vatican-to-recognize-palestinian-state-in-new-treaty.html (''New York Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2015 Burundian unrest]]
**Major General [[Godefroid Niyombare]] has declared a [[Coup d'état|coup]] in Burundi and the establishment of a "national salvation committee". President [[Pierre Nkurunziza]] is attempting to return home from Tanzania. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-32724083 (BBC)]
**Police in Burundi fire on protesters in [[Bujumbura]] opposing the bid by [[President of Burundi|President]] [[Pierre Nkurunziza]] for a third term. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-32717494 (BBC)]
**[[Bujumbura International Airport]] and all land borders are ordered closed by Major General [[Godefroid Niyombare]]. [http://www.news24.com/news24/Africa/News/Burundi-airport-borders-closed-after-coup-attempt-20150513 (AFP via News24)]
** [[Radio Publique Africaine]], one of the most popular radio stations, has been burnt down. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-32732793 BBC]
*The small nation of [[Nauru]] temporarily bans [[Facebook]], purportedly to protect young people. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-05-13/nauru-president-says-internet-facebook-ban-to-protect-children/6465274 (ABC Australia)]
*[[Shooting of Tony Robinson]]: Demonstrators peacefully protest a [[Wisconsin]] prosecutor's decision, announced yesterday, not to pursue charges against the officer who shot and killed a 19-year-old. [http://www.jsonline.com/news/crime/protesters-march-in-madison-day-after-da-declines-to-charge-officer-in-tony-robinson-killing-b994996-303603071.html (''Milwaukee Wisconsin Journal Sentine''l)]

;Politics and elections
*South Korea claims that North Korea has executed its defense chief [[Hyon Yong-chol]] with an [[anti-aircraft gun]]. [http://english.yonhapnews.co.kr/news/2015/05/13/0200000000AEN20150513002800315.html (Yonhap)] [http://edition.cnn.com/2015/05/13/asia/north-korea-executes-defense-chief/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes overwhelmingly to end the mass collection of Americans' phone data with the [[USA Freedom Act]] passing 338-88 (79%). The bill's passage through the [[United States Senate|Senate]] is less certain. [http://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/may/13/nsa-surveillance-congress-usa-freedom-act (''The Guardian'')]

;Sports
*[[Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics]]: The U.S. men's 4x100 metres relay that won a silver medal at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in [[London]] is stripped of the medal due to a positive test result by [[Tyson Gay]]. [https://au.sports.yahoo.com/a/27910455/athletics-usa-tyson-gay-doping-conviction-medals-stripped/ (Reuters via Yahoo 7)]
